item.title: Deezer ramps up fight against AI music fraud
item.description: Deezer has reported a surge in AI-generated music uploads while reinforcing efforts to protect artists’ rights and ensure transparency in streaming. In January 2026, Deezer received an average of 60 000 AI-generated tracks per day, representing approximately 39% of all daily music deliveries. item.title: Ndlovu Youth Choir returns to Cape Town, Joburg with 2026 tour
item.description: The Ndlovu Youth Choir will launch its 2026 national tour with a series of concerts in Cape Town, beginning on 5 February at 7:30pm at the Artscape Theatre Centre. Additional performances will take place on Friday at 7.30pm, at 3pm and 7.30pm, and Sunday at 2pm and 6pm. Johannesburg shows are scheduled for later in the year at Montecasino’s Teatro from 30 July to 2 August. item.title: SA: Kirk Whalum to headline 2026 Gauteng Soul and Jazz concert
item.description: US jazz saxophonist Kirk Whalum will headline the 2026 Gauteng Soul and Jazz Concert, set to take place at Sunbet Arena on 13 June 2026. The event, organised by Remoakantse Holdings, will feature a mix of South African soul, jazz, and Afro-pop artists alongside the Grammy-nominated musician. The line-up includes South African artists Judith Sephuma, Lira, Zonke and Mafikizolo, promising an evening of powerful performances and musical collaborations. item.title: Los Angeles to host live Fela Kuti GRAMMY tribute
item.description: Los Angeles will host a special live band event honouring the late Fela Kuti’s GRAMMY Lifetime Achievement Award at The Paramount on 31 January. The event follows The Recording Academy’s Special Merit Awards Ceremony and aims to celebrate the life, music, and legacy of the Nigerian afrobeat pioneer. item.title: Open call: Pro Helvetia funding for co-creation projects
item.description: Pro Helvetia has opened a call for jointly developed artistic projects that support equal co-creation between artists based in Switzerland and practitioners active in regions covered by Pro Helvetia liaison offices. The call is open to artists working across all disciplines. Target group Artists or cultural practitioners without a connection to Switzerland who are collaborating with a Swiss-based partner. item.title: Sjava completes Inkanyezi Trilogy with new album, announces tour
item.description: South African artist Sjava has released INkanyezi NeZinkanyezi, an album that completes his Inkanyezi trilogy and coincides with the announcement of a national tour marking a decade since his official debut. The album follows the release of two live EPs, Inkanyezi and Inkanyezi 2.0, which were performed and recorded during Sjava’s 2025 tour. item.title: Spotify highlights Africa’s rising artists in NXT playlist
item.description: Spotify has unveiled its NXT – Ones to Watch 2026 playlist, highlighting 50 emerging African artists who are transitioning from early recognition to sustained growth. Positioned between the platform’s Fresh Finds and RADAR Africa playlists, NXT is designed to capture artists at a pivotal stage in their careers, when momentum begins to build across audiences and regions. item.title: Suno appoints ex-Spotify and Patreon executive Sam Berger
item.description: AI music company Suno has appointed music industry executive Sam Berger to expand its artist partnerships operations, as the company continues to strengthen its ties with artists and rights holders. Berger joins Suno following senior roles at Patreon and Spotify, and brings experience across artist management, platform strategy and live music formats. item.title: Nanette pays homage to family and legacy in Abazali
item.description: Nanette’s ‘Abazali’ is a tender and reflective standout from her forthcoming album Painfully Happy. Drawing on the warmth of 1980s Soweto funk and jazz, the song honours family, memory and South Africa’s musical elders. Sung in her home language, it grounds contemporary R&B in lineage and gratitude. The track signals an emotionally generous album rooted in nostalgia, care and cultural continuity. item.title: Grammys 2026: Tyla wins Best African Music Performance
item.description: South African singer Tyla and US-born artist Shaboozey, whose parents are Nigerian, were among the early winners at the 68th Grammy Awards, held at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on 1 February. Tyla won Best African Music Performance for ‘Push 2 Start’, marking another international milestone for the artist following her recent global breakthrough.
